topic: This extends the cross-architecture replication in the first reuse directory above (which already replicated Claims A and B of the paper on Qwen2.5-1.5B base: probe cosine 0.4284 matching Pythia-1.4b reference 0.4283; best steering layer 28 with margin 0.1283 CI[0.1230,0.1337], about 3.2x the Pythia reference of ~0.04, while the passive-best layer 24 also worked at 0.0461). The reuse directory contains the working Qwen-specific pipeline adapters (injection hook location, logit-lens norm module) plus the full baseline/rollout/steering methodology -- reuse this pipeline directly rather than rewriting it, adapting only what differs per model (layer count, hidden dim, exact injection module path). Your task: run the same Claim A (probe vs weak/token-identity/rollout baselines) and Claim B (norm-relative causal steering with a steering-specific multi-layer scan, at least 5 candidate layers spanning early/mid/late, 5 seeds each with 95 percent CI) protocol on TWO more models from the Qwen3 family: Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B. Use the BASE (non-instruct/non-chat) checkpoint for each and explicitly confirm and report that you did so. Use the same reused 600-prompt set, same 549-usable/383-83-83 split with seed 42, and the same all-MiniLM-L6-v2 semantic target for direct comparability. Report results for both models side by side with each other and with the existing references (Pythia-1.4b: probe 0.4283, best steering margin ~0.04; Qwen2.5-1.5b: probe 0.4284, best steering layer 28 margin 0.1283). This gives a within-Qwen-family scaling check (1.7B vs 4B) in addition to the cross-family check already done. GPU 0 only; process one model fully (including deleting its weights cache and large intermediate tensors once its metrics/plots are derived) before starting the next, exactly as the prior run did, to keep disk usage conservative. Produce a report stating clearly whether Claims A and B replicate on both new models, whether results are consistent between Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B (a same-family scaling comparison), and how they compare numerically to the Qwen2.5-1.5B and Pythia-1.4B references.
progress: Cycle 1 review: ACCEPT - The run meets the stated success criteria. The required base model IDs were confirmed and recorded for both Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base. For each model, Claim A artifacts exist and report probe, weak, token-identity, and rollout metrics on the fixed reused setup; in both cases the probe exceeds all listed baselines, satisfying the objective replication threshold for Claim A. For Claim B, both models have scans over at least 5 layers spanning depth, with 5 seeds per layer and 95% CIs; each model has at least one positive best layer whose CI lower bound is above 0, satisfying the objective replication threshold for Claim B. Final comparison tables include both new models plus the two references, and the final report makes explicit binary replication judgments for Claim A and Claim B on each model. Cleanup logs and the summary indicate the required one-model-at-a-time workflow with cleanup before the second model. Although the coder discovered and fixed two implementation/reporting bugs during the process, those were corrected in the final artifacts, and the final delivered experiment appears complete and compliant with the protocol. No further work is needed.
